rationale: C02 supplies an exceptionally close two-sentence template: the first sentence designates a named body as a public international organization entitled to the Act's privileges, exemptions, and immunities; the second preserves privileges already or later acquired by treaty or congressional action. The child changes the organization and slightly recasts "is not intended to abridge" as "shall not be deemed to abridge," while retaining the substance, sequence, and nearly all language. C06 and C14 share the same machinery, but C02 is the closest singular-organization, same-administration formulation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I hereby designate the International Hydrographic Bureau as a public international organization entitled to enjoy the privileges, exemptions, and immunities conferred by the International Organizations Immunities Act.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I hereby designate the World Meteorological Organization as a public international organization entitled to enjoy the privileges, exemptions, and immunities conferred by the said International Organizations Immunities Act.
shared_material.explanation: The operative designation sentence is nearly verbatim, with the named organization substituted and only "said" omitted.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The designation of the International Hydrographic Bureau as a public international organization within the meaning of the International Organizations Immunities Act shall not be deemed to abridge in any respect privileges, exemptions, and immunities which such organization may have acquired or may acquire by treaty or congressional action.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The designation of the World Meteorological Organization as a public international organization within the meaning of the said International Organizations Immunities Act is not intended to abridge in any respect privileges, exemptions, and immunities which such organization may have acquired or may acquire by treaty or congressional action.
shared_material.explanation: The preservation clause retains the same structure and almost identical language, changing only the organization, omitting "said," and replacing "is not intended to" with "shall not be deemed to."
